answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to stake a deposit and build a verifiable work history before earning trust. Each agent emits a signed pulse every round proving it still runs the same workload, and its past attestations accumulate into a relic of reputation that cannot be bought or copied overnight. An attacker spinning up a fable of a thousand fresh identities would have to fund a thousand stakes and sustain a thousand convincing histories, so the cost of forging influence grows with every fake while honest agents pay only once.
